title: Encounter Etiquette
subtitle: Ever try telling a curious creature not to knock your cup off the table?

content.text: Before a shop window on the Champs-Élysées, you stop for a long time, so long you don't notice the sky changing. What you're staring at is:
A Klein-blue gown flowing with black liquid.

branch.text: You have to admit, it's impeccable taste.

content.text: A restored illustration of ancient Critters.
A smoking pipe cut clean in half.

branch.text: Makes you wonder where the other half is shown.

content.text: An astronomical clock with its hands reversed.

branch.text: There must be a deeper metaphor.

content.text: I was running a crystal parlor in Paris back then.
People came for all sorts of products—from ordinary crystal ornaments to the enchanted ones—I had them all. I recognized a few of my customers in your Suitcase.
But many came seeking something I never put on the shelf—prophecy.
I can imagine. Who wouldn't want to know their future?

branch.text: But our path through fate's garden is already set. No prophecy can change where it leads.
And I dislike putting a price on things that have no use.
So I made myself a promise: that only those I trusted would get a glimpse of what lies ahead of them—a gift, nothing more.
I am afraid that was never an option for me. I could never put a price on it. Whether one knows about the future or not, their fate remains unchanged.
A prophecy to fate is like a title to a book, and no bookseller should charge for the title alone.
So, I only offered the gift of prophecy to those who did not come seeking it.
To my surprise, it did something unexpected for my business. Word spread, and I recovered my investment soon enough.
Nor was I. Few things in life have ever surprised me, and this was much the same.

content.text: So you sold prophecies too, then.

items.text: Inside the Taxi
The engine starts, churning into a rhythmic patter as the black taxi moves forward. A chime sways in the taxi—a gift from her parents.

items.speaker: Adèle
items.text: Well, I suppose that's that. No mysterious murderer, just another diviner.

items.speaker: Adèle
items.text: Benjamin said they spoke to her already and cleared her of any suspicion.

items.speaker: Félicienne
items.text: Cleared? I wouldn't be so quick to believe that.

items.speaker: Félicienne
items.text: Beryl Bouanich—she hides herself well, that one.
The passenger pops a pastry into her mouth, chewing with a mix of irritation and thought.

items.speaker: Adèle
items.text: Hm? Do you know her, madame?
Adèle glances over in surprise. She's never seen Félicienne look so displeased.

items.speaker: Félicienne
items.text: This box is empty. Was that the last macaron?

items.speaker: Adèle
items.text: Of course not! I got another box just for you.
She maintains an absolute sense of professionalism while taking out a neatly wrapped box from beside her seat.

items.speaker: Félicienne
items.text: Ah, it seems my expectations have been surpassed, low as they were.

items.speaker: Félicienne
items.text: Mmm. So delicious!

items.speaker: Adèle
items.text: Hah, I must say, you seem to really have a sweet tooth.
The soft crunch of Félicienne biting into a pastry makes Adèle strangely tense. She grips the wheel, forcing herself to focus on the road ahead.

items.speaker: Félicienne
items.text: So, Beryl Bouanich—where is she now? Did your little policeman say anything?

items.speaker: Adèle
items.text: He said she's running a crystal parlor on Rue de la Paix.

items.speaker: Félicienne
items.text: Turn around. I should like to pay her a visit.
A familiar commanding tone comes from the passenger seat. Fortunately, by now, Adèle has learned how to handle it.

items.speaker: Adèle
items.text: Now? I don't know, Félicienne. It's nearly the end of the day.

items.speaker: Adèle
items.text: I'm meeting a friend tonight. I told you that.

items.speaker: Félicienne
items.text: Then you can tell your friend to meet you at Rue de la Paix.
A sharp glare follows the words, audible without even looking at her.

items.speaker: Félicienne
items.text: I'll double your pay for the evening. Turn us around. Take whichever route you like.

items.speaker: Adèle
items.text: But ...

items.speaker: Félicienne
items.text: Ah, fine. Triple? No? Ten times, then.

items.speaker: Adèle
items.text: Ten times?!
Adèle struggles against the temptation but weighs it against what she read in the pamphlets the strikers have been passing around. "Don't be swayed by money alone; workers need rest!"

items.speaker: Adèle
items.text: Ah ... No, Félicienne, I really can't. Célia's always busy these days; I barely get to see her.

items.speaker: Adèle
items.text: She's all wrapped up in this parapsychology thing. I haven't seen her in so long. I don't want to cancel on her.

items.speaker: Adèle
items.text: We'll go to Rue de la Paix tomorrow. I promise.

items.speaker: Félicienne
items.text: You live a terribly tedious life, Adèle Tavernier.
Félicienne narrows her eyes with acute displeasure, but before she can speak, she jerks forward from the passenger seat.

items.speaker: Félicienne
items.text: Wait. Look! That's her!

items.speaker: Adèle
items.text: What? Who?

items.speaker: Félicienne
items.text: Beryl Bouanich! Just there! Turn, now!

items.speaker: Adèle
items.text: Let go! I can turn the wheel my—Rgh!
*screech*
Adèle's car skids in a long arc before finally stopping, while the oncoming vehicle veers into a streetlight.

items.speaker: Agitated Driver
items.text: Damn it! Have you lost your mind?
The driver climbs out, furious, pointing at Adèle as his shouting makes the windows rattle.

items.speaker: Agitated Driver
items.text: Ah! I'm speaking to you! Out of the car! Now!

items.speaker: Félicienne
items.text: What are you staring at? You heard the man. Get out.

items.speaker: Adèle
items.text: We'll settle this later!
Pushing open the door, Adèle silently praises her own quick reflexes. The crash isn't too severe.
There's no sign of anyone like Beryl Bouanich on the street. The whole thing just feels like another stroke of bad luck on the drive home.

items.speaker: Adèle
items.text: What was she thinking? Urgh, ah, grabbing the wheel like that! Never imagined my first crash would be like this.
She rubs her forehead and steels herself to face the fuming young man nearby.

items.speaker: Adèle
items.text: I'm terribly sorry, sir. I was distracted—

items.speaker: Agitated Driver
items.text: Sorry? Aha! Do you even have the slightest clue what sort of damage you've caused?

items.speaker: Agitated Driver
items.text: We can't afford to lose time here! The nation is calling to us!
He slams his fist against his own car. The already-dented trunk lets out a hollow, miserable groan as the crowd thickens.

items.speaker: Adèle
items.text: Ah? The nation?

items.speaker: Adèle
items.text: Is that a strike slogan? Or do you mean you have urgent business to tend to?

items.speaker: Agitated Driver
items.text: Our one true leader has returned! The Emperor has landed at Golfe-Juan! He will bring glory to France once more!

items.speaker: Agitated Driver
items.text: He's riding to Paris with only a few hundred soldiers at his side. Our Emperor is too distant from his people. We must go to him!

items.speaker: Adèle
items.text: The Emperor? Golfe-Juan? What on earth are you talking about?
The man's stern face makes it clear he isn't joking. Adèle stares at him, at a loss for words.
But her silence seems to be taken another way.

items.speaker: Agitated Driver
items.text: I see. You've sided with the Bourbons, haven't you? You're another one of the king's stooges!

items.speaker: Agitated Driver
items.text: The Sun of Austerlitz calls to me. I will not be stopped!

items.speaker: Agitated Driver
items.text: Let me be! I must go to the Emperor!

items.speaker: Adèle
items.text: Sir, calm yourself! Someone help me, please!
With help from the bystanders, Adèle manages to pull the driver down from the roof, though the commotion draws even more onlookers.

items.speaker: Curious Passerby I
items.text: Ay, ay, ay! Another poor fellow lost in delusion.

items.speaker: Curious Passerby II
items.text: Careful! Don't get too close. He's talking gibberish. The Hundred Days ended over a hundred years ago.

items.speaker: Adèle
items.text: Please, someone, get him to the hospital. He needs help!

items.speaker: Adèle
items.text: Does anyone know this man? I really need to go. I have to see someone.
She looks at her scratched-up car and the indifferent lady inside, feeling a twinge of helplessness.
Just then, the crowd parts as several men in scholarly attire push their way forward.
Vincent, my God! I'm terribly sorry for all the trouble he's caused, miss! He's my student. Please, allow me to cover the damages.
Would you mind leaving me your address? I'll take care of the rest.
A man in his forties finally makes it through, wiping sweat from his brow with a handkerchief. His face full of apology.
Several young people follow behind him—students, led by a girl Adèle immediately recognizes.

items.speaker: Adèle
items.text: Célia!

items.speaker: Célia
items.text: Adèle? Goodness, are you hurt?
She rushes over, checking that Adèle and the driver are safe before stepping back and introducing the others.

items.speaker: Célia
items.text: This is Professor Roseau—the one I told you about. Professor, this is my friend, Adèle.

items.speaker: Célia
items.text: She's who I was going to see this evening.
Célia finishes her introductions, patting her friend's shoulder in relief.

items.speaker: Célia
items.text: Thank goodness you stopped him, Adèle! Who knows what might have happened otherwise.

items.speaker: Professor Roseau
items.text: Yes, yes. You acted both quickly and rightly, miss.
Faced with unexpected thanks, Adèle scratches her head, trying to shift the topic back to the still-babbling driver.

items.speaker: Adèle
items.text: Uh ... What's wrong with him?

items.speaker: Célia
items.text: It's a long story. He's been acting strange for weeks.

items.speaker: Célia
items.text: So when he didn't turn up this morning, we went to his home to check on him. The door was open, and it was a total mess.

items.speaker: Professor Roseau
items.text: Poor boy. Such potential. But then perhaps I pushed him too hard.
The man cuts Célia off, shaking his head, guilt written all over his face.

items.speaker: Professor Roseau
items.text: I shan't keep you, ladies. Célia, go with your friend. I'll deal with all this.

items.speaker: Célia
items.text: But ...

items.speaker: Professor Roseau
items.text: Please, Célia. Put this behind you and enjoy your evening. But be sure to join me for tomorrow's fieldwork.
She glances at Adèle, then accepts her teacher's offer.
After helping the poor man away, the crowd gradually disperses as night falls over the street.

items.speaker: Célia
items.text: How's your car? I know the professor said he'd cover it.

items.speaker: Adèle
items.text: Not bad, just a dent on the bumper. It was a bit of a fright, but I'm fine now.

items.speaker: Adèle
items.text: Ah, wait! Sorry, Célia, I need to—
The whirlwind of events leaves Adèle dizzy. She finally regains her senses and runs toward her Peugeot 201 parked nearby.

items.speaker: Adèle
items.text: Félicienne's still in the car! I'll have to take her back to the hotel.

items.speaker: Adèle
items.text: Urh. She's not going to be happy after I left her like that.

items.speaker: Adèle
items.text: Félicienne! Fé—huh?
The passenger seat is vacant, replaced by a line of bright red words scrawled across the window.
Tomorrow, Rue de la Paix.

items.speaker: Adèle
items.text: Oh, no. Is that lipstick?!
Adèle pulls out a handkerchief to wipe the writing from the glass, but despite her scrubbing, it barely fades.

items.speaker: Adèle
items.text: First she grabs the wheel, crashing my car, might I add. And then, she has the cheek to scribble on the window! Ugh! She's paying for a full clean, I swear it!

items.speaker: Célia
items.text: Are you certain you're alright?
Her friend walks over, peeking curiously through the window.
Adèle waves it off, refusing to let this small incident ruin their long-awaited dinner.

items.speaker: Adèle
items.text: Ugh! I'm fine. *exhale* So, shall we eat at that spot near the Seine again, or are you feeling adventurous tonight?

items.speaker: Adèle
items.text: You said you couldn't stand the campus cafés anymore. So, tonight, my darling, you choose the food.

items.speaker: Célia
items.text: Really? I suppose if I could have anything ... You know, what I'm really missing is some good home cooking.
She starts counting on her fingers, reciting a whole list of dishes.

items.speaker: Célia
items.text: Onion soup, gratin dauphinois, maybe a bit of cheese for a small fondue. Oh, and I just bought a bottle of cider. What do you think?

items.speaker: Célia
items.text: You simply have to come over and see my place now. I cleaned the whole thing. Balcony, too! I came over to ask you for help, but you weren't home.

items.speaker: Adèle
items.text: Home cooking it is! Hop in!
In perfect sync, the two circle to opposite sides of the Peugeot 201 and open the doors at once.

items.speaker: Adèle
items.text: Buckle up, to home!
